candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity client-needs subcategory (6–12% of items); this item tests assessment of mood and coping, therapeutic support, social functioning, and coordination of psychosocial resources in chronic illness.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial assessment, coping support, and resource coordination during chronic illness
candidate.educational_objective: Support psychological adjustment to chronic respiratory disease through ongoing assessment of mood, coping, safety, and social functioning and by coordinating individualized psychosocial and rehabilitation resources rather than assuming emotional needs end when medical treatment stabilizes.

options.A: Assess mood, coping, safety, social functioning, and support needs; provide ongoing emotional support and coordinate appropriate pulmonary-rehabilitation, social-work, or mental-health resources
options.B: Limit follow-up to medication adherence because psychosocial concerns no longer require assessment once respiratory treatment is stable
options.C: Explain that social withdrawal is an expected consequence of chronic lung disease and does not require further evaluation
options.D: Wait until the client specifically requests psychiatric treatment before acknowledging mood or adjustment concerns

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current American Thoracic Society pulmonary-rehabilitation guidance defines rehabilitation as a comprehensive, patient-tailored intervention intended to improve both physical and psychological condition in chronic respiratory disease. ATS pulmonary-rehabilitation resources explicitly include psychosocial support within integrated care. Current NCBI/StatPearls pulmonary-rehabilitation guidance likewise emphasizes that progressive lung disease has important psychological and social effects, that anxiety and depression should be assessed, and that psychologists and social workers may be incorporated when needed. B, C, and D dismiss clinically meaningful mood, coping, and social-function changes that warrant assessment and individualized support.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current ATS and NCBI resources directly support integrating ongoing psychological and social assessment and support into chronic respiratory-disease care and using multidisciplinary rehabilitation or mental-health resources when indicated.
candidate.source_document_title: Pulmonary Rehabilitation for Adults with Chronic Respiratory Disease: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline; Pulmonary Rehabilitation

candidate.stem: A client with chronic respiratory disease says, "I have stopped seeing friends because the illness has changed so much of my life, and I feel down most days." Which nursing action is most appropriate?
